subject: Incident comms templates — final review + signoff (Support/CS)
body:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwoodinference.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia_benson@redwoodinference.com>, Wei Chen <wei_chen@redwoodinference.com>, Elliot Price <elliot_price@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Nov 12, 2025 at 9:08 AM PT
Subject: Incident comms templates — final review + signoff (Support/CS)
Attachments: Incident_Comms_Templates_v1.3.docx; Statuspage_Update_Tone_Guide_v0.9.pdf

Dev / Jasmine / Rachel —

We’re at final wording for the status page incident update templates (Investigating / Identified / Mitigating / Monitoring / Resolved) as part of the Status Page Transparency upgrades.

Request: Support/CS signoff today so we can lock copy and proceed with training + macros updates (INT-10430).

What changed since v1.2:
- Clearer “what we know vs what we’re doing” split in Investigating.
- Explicit guardrails: no SLA language, no customer-specific capacity details.
- Dedicated/Private guidance: what we can say publicly when impact is isolated to a single tenant/environment.
- Added a standard line to set expectations on next update timing without overcommitting.

Ask:
1) Confirm you’re comfortable with the wording, especially:
   - “Some customers” vs “a subset of requests” phrasing
   - When we say “degraded performance” vs “partial outage”
   - The escalation handoff sentence to Support (“If you need help, contact Support…”) 
2) Confirm who approves public updates for Sev0/Sev1 after the optional approval step lands (Support lead vs IC).

If we get a “yes” by EOD, we’ll publish to Confluence + roll into incident-bot drafts this week.

Thanks,
Sean
—
Sean Gallagher
Director, Site Reliability Engineering
Redwood Inference



From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwoodinference.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia_benson@redwoodinference.com>, Wei Chen <wei_chen@redwoodinference.com>, Elliot Price <elliot_price@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Nov 12, 2025 at 10:02 AM PT
Subject: Re: Incident comms templates — final review + signoff (Support/CS)

Reviewed. Overall looks good and matches what we need for ticket deflection.

Edits/notes from Support Ops:
- In Investigating, can we avoid “Some customers are unable to…” and instead use “A subset of requests are failing…”? We’ve seen customers interpret “some customers” as “we know who you are / we’re singling you out.”
- For “next update,” I like the phrasing but suggest: “We’ll provide an update within 30–60 minutes” (range) rather than “within 60 minutes.” When we miss “within 60,” it creates more tickets.
- Add one sentence in Resolved that Support can reuse: “If you’re still seeing issues, please contact Support with request IDs and timestamps.”

Approval flow: for Sev0/Sev1, I’d like Support lead approval for the first public update when the incident appears customer-visible but facts are still uncertain. After that, IC/Comms Lead can proceed.

If Wei can incorporate the copy tweaks, I’m comfortable signing off.

Dev
—
Dev Patel
Director, Support Operations
Redwood Inference



From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia_benson@redwoodinference.com>, Wei Chen <wei_chen@redwoodinference.com>, Elliot Price <elliot_price@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Nov 12, 2025 at 10:27 AM PT
Subject: Re: Incident comms templates — final review + signoff (Support/CS)

+1 to Dev’s notes.

Two additional CS items:
- Dedicated/Private: we should be careful with “We’re not seeing impact to all customers.” For an enterprise customer in Dedicated, that can read as dismissive. Prefer: “We’re investigating reports of impact; scope is still being determined.”
- Can we standardize on “requests” vs “API calls”? Some customers use non-HTTP language and “requests” is neutral.

Otherwise, I’m aligned.

Jasmine
—
Jasmine Liu
Head of Customer Success
Redwood Inference



From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia_benson@redwoodinference.com>, Wei Chen <wei_chen@redwoodinference.com>, Elliot Price <elliot_price@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Nov 12, 2025 at 11:03 AM PT
Subject: Re: Incident comms templates — final review + signoff (Support/CS)

Adding a small request from Enterprise CS:

In Identified/Mitigating, can we avoid naming internal systems (e.g., “scheduler,” “gateway”) unless it’s customer-facing? We’ve had security reviews where those get screenshotted and reinterpreted.

Suggestion: keep it to “a backend dependency” / “inference routing” / “streaming connection handling” depending on capability.

If we can apply that consistently, I’m a yes.

Rachel
—
Rachel Kim
Enterprise Customer Success
Redwood Inference



From: Wei Chen <wei_chen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwoodinference.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia_benson@redwoodinference.com>, Elliot Price <elliot_price@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Nov 12, 2025 at 12:18 PM PT
Subject: Re: Incident comms templates — final review + signoff (Support/CS)

I can incorporate all of the above today.

Proposed changes (will update v1.3 -> v1.4 in Confluence):
- Replace “Some customers…” with “A subset of requests…” across phases.
- Next update line becomes: “We’ll provide another update within 30–60 minutes, or sooner if we have new information.”
- Resolved adds: “If you’re still seeing issues, contact Support and include request IDs + timestamps.”
- Dedicated/Private: remove “not seeing impact to all customers” language; use “scope still being determined.”
- Remove internal system names; keep capability-level references only.

One question for Sean/Rafael: do we want the Investigating template to include a sentence about mitigations in progress (“we’re applying mitigations”) or keep it strictly to investigation until we’re confident?

Wei
—
Wei Chen
Customer Communications (Product)
Redwood Inference



From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Wei Chen <wei_chen@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwoodinference.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia_benson@redwoodinference.com>, Elliot Price <elliot_price@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Nov 12, 2025 at 2:06 PM PT
Subject: Re: Incident comms templates — final review + signoff (Support/CS)

Legal review notes (light-touch):
- Avoid definitive causation statements until confirmed (e.g., “caused by”). Prefer “related to” / “due to an issue in” / “we believe the issue is associated with.”
- Avoid commitments framed as guarantees (“will be resolved”). Fine to say “we’re working to restore” and “we’re seeing signs of recovery.”

No objections otherwise. Thanks for keeping these publishable and not overly specific.

Michael Grant
Legal (Commercial)
Redwood Inference



From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwoodinference.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia_benson@redwoodinference.com>, Wei Chen <wei_chen@redwoodinference.com>, Elliot Price <elliot_price@redwoodinference.com>, Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Nov 12, 2025 at 4:47 PM PT
Subject: Re: Incident comms templates — final review + signoff (Support/CS)

Thanks all — we’ll take the edits as written.

Decisions:
- Wording: adopt Wei’s proposed v1.4 changes + Michael’s causation/commitment guardrails.
- Investigating template: include mitigation language only if we’re actively taking a customer-impacting action (e.g., failover, rollback, capacity shift). Otherwise keep it to investigation + verification.
- Approval flow (Sev0/Sev1): first public update requires either (a) Support lead approval (Dev or delegate) OR (b) IC approval if Support is unavailable within 10 minutes. Subsequent updates can be owned by Comms Lead + IC.

Training:
- Comms Lead / IC training #1: Tue 11/19 10:00–10:45am PT
- Comms Lead / IC training #2: Thu 11/21 2:00–2:45pm PT
Talia will send invites; Elliot/Wei will be on to walk through examples + what not to say.

Next steps:
- Wei: update Confluence page to v1.4 today and ping this thread with the link.
- Dev: align INT-10430 support macros with the final templates.
- Rafael: ensure incident-bot draft generator points at v1.4 copy.

Signing off from SRE.

Sean
—
Sean Gallagher
Director, Site Reliability Engineering
Redwood Inference
